end.parentNote: Asha practised equal sharing, finding fractions of collections, and comparing unit fractions. Nisha used equal-grouping and division for 15 pencils and 9 sticks; the idea became clear after revisiting the examples. Nisha first mixed up whether 1/3 or 1/2 is larger, then corrected this by using sharing examples: fewer equal parts make larger pieces. At home, share 6 or 12 small objects into 2, 3, and 4 equal groups and ask which one-third, one-half, or one-quarter is larger.
